morphology: Deep narrow primary and shallow narrow secondary with an eccentric phase separation. Individual primary branches drift on the Gaia-period fold.
visual_attribution: S99 has a compact deficit. The initial S65 blue spot is a real sign error at the old phase. The TESS timing fit restores 4/4 positive events in both S65 and S99, phase controls below 1 ppt. The 23 arcsec fainter neighbour needs its own hypothesis test.

morphology: Two sharp unequal dips on a gently modulated continuum. Primary branches broaden at the Gaia period.
visual_attribution: S24 and S85 show compact repeat deficits at the marked position. The nearby brighter field structure does not coincide with either peak. A 10 arcsec neighbour 3.5 mag down is unresolved in the static image.

morphology: Two sharply bounded dips, different depths, on a double-wave continuum.
visual_attribution: Several separated bright stars are visible. Neither bright comparison star dims in the S16/S84 deficit stamps. The strongest compact deficit lands at the target twice.

morphology: Deep flat-bottomed dip with separated tracks on the Gaia-period fold. Baseline modulation is shallow relative to the eclipse.
visual_attribution: S17/S85 have a compact peak on broad sky structure. The refitted locally corrected aperture reproduces 14/14 positive events. A 7.95 arcsec neighbour only 0.63 mag down shares the PSF. The target's Gaia G/BP/RP epochs dim at three TESS-predicted visits, one with the noisy-data flag clear. Its neighbour lacks public epochs.
visual_conclusion: target favoured by Gaia; TESS close blend

morphology: Deep narrow flat-bottomed primary drifts across phase in the unrefined fold. Weak modulation persists outside the dip.
visual_attribution: S6/S32 show repeated centrally concentrated deficits. An out-of-aperture bright star remains quiet in the stamps. The S6 deficit centre is displaced about a third of a pixel; S32 is closer.

morphology: Shallow narrow primary on low-level undulations. A single binned minimum is clear against the noisy continuum.
visual_attribution: S19 has an isolated positive peak near target. The initial S86 stamp has a sky pedestal and a large negative aperture outlier. Local subtraction recovers all 14 S19/S86 events. A 3.77 arcsec neighbour shares the pixel. Matched Gaia G/BP/RP core visits show the target fading much more than that neighbour. Both have noisy-data warnings on both visits.
visual_conclusion: target favoured by paired Gaia photometry; TESS close blend

morphology: Two nearly equal narrow V-shaped eclipses separated by about half a cycle, on ellipsoidal modulation.
visual_attribution: Both S16 and S84 have compact deficits at the marked star. The separate field source remains quiet in the difference frames.
visual_conclusion: target favoured; equal dips limit photometric period discrimination

morphology: Two very deep eclipses with similar depths. Individual tracks separate slightly on the displayed period. Shallow baseline modulation is present.
visual_attribution: S36/S90 place compact strong deficits on the target, distinct from the separated brighter field stars.

morphology: Narrow attenuated primary over noisy, structured out-of-eclipse variability. The alternate conjunction lacks a comparable trough in this fold.
visual_attribution: S7 has a compact positive peak on the faint target. S61 has broad sky structure and an extreme aperture outlier in its original mean. Event-local sky subtraction gives 9/9 dimmings across sectors. The bright off-axis star stays separated.

morphology: Twin sharply bounded dips on a double-wave baseline. Sector-dependent phase displacement is visible before period refinement.
visual_attribution: Both S9 and S63 give a high-contrast deficit near the central bright source. The out-of-event image is extended; target and difference maximum agree within the central pixel.

morphology: Narrow shallow primary and no obvious corresponding deep secondary. The original fold gives a compact core and a sloping shelf on its late side.
visual_attribution: Original S26/S80 differences have strong backgrounds. The event-local aperture reproduces five dimmings near 18?19 ppt. S26 gives one off-phase control depth of 9.9 ppt; all four S80 controls stay below 1 ppt. A faint source lies 18 arcsec away and a brighter alternative 20.6 arcsec away. Transit morphology alone cannot establish the companion type.
visual_conclusion: target favoured; classification and blend caveats

morphology: Two narrow sharp dips of unequal depth. A broad asymmetric brightening precedes the eclipse toward the edge of the fold.
visual_attribution: S54/S81 show isolated strong deficits centred at the target. Two events per sector. The broad brightening does not dominate the local difference images.

morphology: Two distinct narrow dips separated by roughly a quarter of the cycle; primary is deeper. Sector-dependent primary depth and baseline are evident on the original fold.
visual_attribution: S37/S100 deficits concentrate on the faint target and separate from the brighter field neighbour. S37 has only one usable image event; S100 has two.

morphology: Narrow near-equal double dips with two groups of points per eclipse in the original Gaia-period fold, consistent with accumulating phase error.
visual_attribution: S54/S81 show high-contrast compact deficits at the marked source. Multiple clean events accompany the sector aggregates.

morphology: Deep sharply bounded primary, much shallower secondary, small baseline structure. Primary is well traced by densely sampled data.
visual_attribution: S47/S60 deficit maxima track the target pixel. Comparable large aperture depths recur through both sectors.
